title: Nuremberg-style Lebkuchen
summary: Soft, flourless nut-and-spice Christmas cookies in the Elisen style, glazed with dark chocolate.

ingredients.note: 16 whole blanched almonds, for the tops; optional

steps: Beat the eggs with the erythritol and allulose for 5 minutes, until thick and pale.
Fold in the almond and hazelnut flours, zests, spices, baking powder and salt. The mixture will be soft. Cover and leave 1 hour so the nuts absorb the moisture and the spices bloom.
Heat the oven to 160 °C (325 °F) and line two baking sheets with parchment.
With wet hands, shape 16 mounds about 6 cm (2½ in) across and 1.5 cm (½ in) high. Press an almond into any you are not glazing.
Bake 15–18 minutes, until the edges are firm and the tops just coloured; the centres stay soft. Cool completely.
Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil and brush or spoon it over the cooled cookies. Leave to set.
tips: Traditional Elisenlebkuchen are baked on thin wafers called Oblaten, which contain starch; parchment does the job here.
Stored airtight for a few days, they soften and the spice deepens.

origin.history: Honey-and-spice cakes were made in German monasteries in the Middle Ages, and Nuremberg, a hub of the spice trade, became famous for them; the city's Lebkuchen bakers are recorded from the late medieval period. The richest kind, Elisenlebkuchen, is made almost entirely of nuts with little or no flour.
